results.title: Rock Core Orientation Technology Using Resistivity Method v1
results.abstract: Restoring the original orientation of core samples in the formation is crucial for geological engineers to better understand the physical properties of subsurface rocks, holding significant importance for engineering operations such as hydraulic fracturing design. However, over 99% of cores worldwide are acquired via conventional drilling coring, making it difficult to determine their orientation during the trip out of the hole. While directional coring and cutting core into cubes for paleomagnetic testing aim to achieve core orientation, the complexity of these processes prevents their widespread use on most cores. To address this, this paper develops an electrical resistivity-based core orientation technique suitable for the more universally available cylindrical cores. It obtains resistivity scanning images of the core, which are then meticulously correlated with downhole electrical imaging logging results. This enables core orientation, providing exploration professionals with the means to gain geological insights incorporating directional information.
